lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Launch and diagnostic: asking for clarification

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic asking for clarification task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: The learner watches for one real moment this week when someone they live with gives a task or direction that leaves out an important detail, such as which item, how much, or by when, and asks a specific clarifying question before starting instead of guessing.

simulationAlternative.description: If no real ambiguous instruction comes up this week, the learner instead writes a short imagined script: one vague instruction a household member might realistically give, the specific clarifying question the learner would ask in response, a plausible answer to that question, and what the learner would do next with that information.

materials: learner-local: paper or a notes app

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g7-u04-l01-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g7-u04-l01-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g7-u04-l01-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g7-u04-l01-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: Explain whether asking your clarifying question changed the outcome compared to guessing, and describe one specific way you would phrase your next clarifying question differently.

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g7-u04-l01-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g7-u04-l01-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g7-u04-l01-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Clarifying question specificity: The question names the exact missing detail (which one, how much, by when, or similar) tied to a real instruction. | Real-world outcome reporting: The real instruction, the specific question asked, and the other person's response are all reported. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g7-u04-l01-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner keep a running log of every clarifying question they ask a household member for one full week and compare how often asking prevented a mistake to how often it wouldn't have mattered either way.

productionDepth.practicalGoal: I can complete a realistic asking for clarification task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.

duration.elapsedWindow: Up to seven days; use only the check-ins explicitly named in the task
duration.sessionPattern: 8–10 minutes model and planning, 8–10 minutes guided try, 20–30 minutes application, 7–10 minutes evidence and revision
duration.adultTime: No adult time required unless the learner chooses support

localMaterials.label: paper or a notes app
localMaterials.availabilityRule: Use only when already available, safe, permitted, and appropriate. The complete fictional route replaces unavailable real-world access.

materials.noPurchaseRule: No purchase is required. Use the complete fictional route when a local material, setting, source, or adult is unavailable.

resources.title: asking for clarification worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: The learner watches for one real moment this week when someone they live with gives a task or direction that leaves out an important detail, such as which item, how much, or by when, and asks a specific clarifying question before starting instead of guessing.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact asking for clarification decision or action.
Model move 2: Think back to a recent time you were given an instruction that was missing an important detail.
Model move 3: Practice turning a vague direction into a specific clarifying question that names exactly what information is missing.

Model check: Clarifying question specificity: The question names the exact missing detail (which one, how much, by when, or similar) tied to a real instruction. | Real-world outcome reporting: The real instruction, the specific question asked, and the other person's response are all reported.

resources.title: asking for clarification action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal, constraints, and privacy boundary for asking for clarification.
2. Analyze the worked model and identify why its sequence meets the criteria.
3. Complete the guided case and use feedback before moving on.
4. Select the permitted real-life route or the complete fictional route.
5. Carry out the task, retaining only the minimum evidence named in the record.
6. Compare the result with the success checks and complete the correction loop when needed.

resources.title: asking for clarification coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: The learner watches for one real moment this week when someone they live with gives a task or direction that leaves out an important detail, such as which item, how much, or by when, and asks a specific clarifying question before starting instead of guessing.
Coach direction: Think back to a recent time you were given an instruction that was missing an important detail.
Learner prompt: Describe one instruction you received recently that left out a detail you needed, and what you did instead of asking (guessed, assumed, or did nothing).
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: asking for clarification complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Practice turning a vague direction into a specific clarifying question that names exactly what information is missing.
Response 1 (t2-p1): I wrote down one real vague or incomplete direction I've received.
Response 2 (t2-p2): I wrote a specific question that names exactly what information is missing, not just a general 'what do you mean?'

Equal-access rule: If no real ambiguous instruction comes up this week, the learner instead writes a short imagined script: one vague instruction a household member might realistically give, the specific clarifying question the learner would ask in response, a plausible answer to that question, and what the learner would do next with that information.

resources.title: asking for clarification minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Explain whether asking your clarifying question changed the outcome compared to guessing, and describe one specific way you would phrase your next clarifying question differently.

Success checks: Clarifying question specificity: The question names the exact missing detail (which one, how much, by when, or similar) tied to a real instruction. | Real-world outcome reporting: The real instruction, the specific question asked, and the other person's response are all reported.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: asking for clarification supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g7-u04-l01-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g7-u04-l01-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional asking for clarification condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Clarifying question specificity: The question names the exact missing detail (which one, how much, by when, or similar) tied to a real instruction. | Real-world outcome reporting: The real instruction, the specific question asked, and the other person's response are all reported..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g7-u04-l01-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

guidedFirstAttempt.setup: The learner watches for one real moment this week when someone they live with gives a task or direction that leaves out an important detail, such as which item, how much, or by when, and asks a specific clarifying question before starting instead of guessing.
guidedFirstAttempt.prompt: Describe one instruction you received recently that left out a detail you needed, and what you did instead of asking (guessed, assumed, or did nothing).
coachMoves: Ask the learner to name the condition.
Point to one model step only.
Give feedback against one observable success check.
guidedFirstAttempt.successCondition: Clarifying question specificity: The question names the exact missing detail (which one, how much, by when, or similar) tied to a real instruction.
guidedFirstAttempt.correctionTurn: Use the fresh condition on swk-rfl-g7-u04-l01-guided-card: change one constraint, redo only the affected move, and state why the corrected move now meets the success check.

realRoute.title: asking for clarification — permitted real-life route
realRoute.permissionRule: Use only a safe, permitted setting and the materials already available to you.
steps: Confirm the setting, materials, and stop condition before acting.
Practice turning a vague direction into a specific clarifying question that names exactly what information is missing.
Complete the response prompts on the delivered independent card without recording private identifying details.
Check the result against the delivered evidence record and correct any missed step.
realRoute.completionCondition: The learner submits the minimal process record and the completed application responses.

simulationRoute.title: asking for clarification — complete fictional route
simulationRoute.directions: If no real ambiguous instruction comes up this week, the learner instead writes a short imagined script: one vague instruction a household member might realistically give, the specific clarifying question the learner would ask in response, a plausible answer to that question, and what the learner would do next with that information.
simulationRoute.completionCondition: Complete the same decision, procedure, evidence, and revision checks as the real-life route. No adult attests that a physical event occurred.

independentTask.privacyAlternative: The learner may use invented names, dates, amounts, organizations, spaces, and circumstances whenever real details are unnecessary or private.

retry.trigger: Start the correction loop when a required step is missing, the reason does not match the condition, a safety or privacy boundary is crossed, or the evidence does not show the stated result.
retry.targetedReteach: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g7-u04-l01-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step.
retry.supportedReattempt: Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g7-u04-l01-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check.
retry.feedback: Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments.
retry.parallelReattempt: Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g7-u04-l01-retry-pair without the coach prompt.
retry.exitCriterion: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Clarifying question specificity: The question names the exact missing detail (which one, how much, by when, or similar) tied to a real instruction. | Real-world outcome reporting: The real instruction, the specific question asked, and the other person's response are all reported.
retry.returnPath: Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g7-u04-l01-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.

guardianInvolvement.role: Optional coach only; no guardian attestation is required.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
